speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the current rate of real wage growth in Singapore; (b) given rising cost of living concerns, what is the forecast for real wage growth for 2023 and how does this compare to previous years; and (c) what measures are being considered to support businesses in ensuring real wage growth for their employees.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the cumulative impact of the series of price increases on wage growth; and (b) in light of these increases, whether there are concerns about the possibility of stagnating wage growth particularly for vulnerable Singapore workers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the real median income growth has kept pace with inflation over the past five years; (b) whether the latest data on real median income growth is within the Ministry’s expected range; and (c) whether there is a need for more stratified and sectoral data points considering the impact of the recent price increases on certain vulnerable groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But let me first talk more broadly about the wage outcomes before I come back to the income growth of lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: While the economic outlook remains uncertain, we expect inflation to moderate for the rest of the year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In its recent announcement on 31 October, the National Wages Council (NWC) has called on employers to consider giving a one-off special lump sum payment to workers in recognition of the impact of high prices.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The NWC Guidelines recommend that employers reward workers fairly based on their contributions and overall business performance, and adopt the Flexible Wage System in order to stay nimble and responsive amidst economic uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To Mr Chia’s question, our strategy to sustain real income growth is to continue to raise productivity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is why we have embarked on the 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) to transform businesses and upskill workers for jobs of the future across the economy.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The NWC has also reiterated its call to employers to press on with transformation and upskilling to ensure that income growth is sustainable, and the Government will support such efforts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Employers can make use of the 16 Jobs Transformation Maps which provide actionable roadmaps to redesign jobs and upskill workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Employers can also tap on programmes such as Workforce Singapore’s Career Conversion Programmes, which provide up to 90% salary and course subsidies, to reskill their existing workers to take on enhanced job roles or train mid-career new hires to take on new roles.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As indicated in the Forward Singapore report, we will launch new career health initiatives to improve job matching and help Singaporeans better plan for their long-term careers, through access to better data and information about jobs and skills.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will enhance employers’ access to talent and ensure better labour market outcomes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Saktiandi and Mr Chia would be pleased to know that lower-wage workers have experienced good real income growth over the last five years.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This means that as costs of living rose, the incomes of lower-wage workers rose even more, thereby narrowing the income gap between lower-wage workers and the median worker.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have recently expanded the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) to cover more lower-wage workers, and this will boost their incomes even further over the next few years – workers covered by PWM can expect cumulative wage increases of up to 80% by 2028.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Amid a tight labour market, lower-wage workers who are not directly covered by PWM should also see meaningful wage increases, as employers will have to respond to market forces to attract and retain workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To reduce the impact on employers, the Government co-funds up to 75% of wage increases given by employers to eligible lower-wage workers from 2022 to 2026, through the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: PWCS will soften the cost impact on employers in the near term, and give employers time to invest in upskilling workers and improving firm-level productivity so that the wage increases are sustainable.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Government also enhanced the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme in January 2023 to further boost the income of lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will be further enhancing Workfare as shared by Prime Minister Lee at the National Day Rally 2023 and details will be shared at next year’s Budget.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: First, can he highlight sectors or jobs that are most at risk of wage stagnation or even worse, further deterioration in their wages?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Second, what are the reasons for the elevated risks in these jobs or sectors?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And third, what further support will the Government put in place to support employers in these sectors?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: However, as overall wage growth is projected to moderate, it could remain elevated in several sectors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Wage increments are expected to stay firm in travel-related sectors where demand continues to recover, as well as more labour intensive services sectors where manpower shortages could be more persistent.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If we think about it, the decline in real income in the first half of 2023 compared to the first half of 2022 was due to elevated inflation, rather than just wage decline.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have to look at real income in that context.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Overall, what we see is that the decline in real income was broad-based and not so much specific to certain sectors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And in terms of the nominal income change, you would also see that across various sectors, the changes did not outpace inflation, and therefore, you see the decline in real incomes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For the strategy to help businesses, we do need to support efforts to raise productivity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It goes beyond just increasing wages because there is impact on business costs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If productivity is not raised, you will find that businesses cannot sustain the wage increases.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have to look at that and balance both the impact of inflation and also look to see how we can improve productivity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is where we can work together in the next couple of years to improve wage outcomes, as a whole.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Do support us, do work with the Government in areas such as the Career Conversion Programmes for workers, Support for Job Redesign under Productivity Solutions Grant and the SkillsFuture credits.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are among the schemes that businesses can tap on.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, the Senior Minister of State shared briefly about the median income growth outlook over the next year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can he share a bit of it in the near term, for example, over the next five years, for example?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, given concerns of higher inflation over a longer time, if it does happen, can the Senior Minister of State share a bit more about the strategies for middle-income, lower middle-income and slightly upper middle-income workers?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And lower middle- and middle-income Singaporeans will eventually become vulnerable groups if they lose their job or fall sick.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, can the Senior Minister of State share a bit more on that, please?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: My crystal ball does not go that far.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I shared earlier, if we look at the trend for the rest of the year and if inflation moderates, that means the situation with the declines in real income will potentially moderate.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, let us not forget that in the last five years, we have seen good improvements with regard to real income.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, we have to take some of these things into account.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The same goes for our lower-wage workers too today, where although they have the PWM, it is really about helping companies transform and redesign jobs so that we can sustain the wage increases.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Otherwise, wage increases without corresponding productivity growth will be challenging, not just for the businesses but our economy as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Firm-level productivity improvements have to continue as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, at the worker level, you need skills and productivity improvements as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I will take it at all three levels for us to sustain the wage growth in coming years.
